detail.longDescription: I'm running a hybrid k3s cluster (Hetzner Cloud CX23 nodes + Proxmox VMs on a dedicated server, connected via Hetzner vSwitch VLAN). Storage is local-path-provisioner (node-local PVs, no network storage). PostgreSQL HA is managed by the Zalando postgres-operator (Patroni, using the Kubernetes API as DCS). The problem: Failover works fine when I kill the primary pod directly — Patroni detects it and promotes a replica within seconds. But when the node hosting the primary pod goes down entirely (power-off / network partition, not a clean drain), failover does not trigger reliably: The primary pod stays "Running" from Kubernetes' perspective for the full node-monitor-grace-period before being marked NotReady/evicted Patroni's leader lease (stored as a K8s ConfigMap/Endpoint) doesn't get released until that eviction happens Meanwhile no replica takes over — the cluster is down for several minutes minimum Since I use local-path (node-local, not network-backed), the dead node's PV is obviously gone with it — but even the promotion of an existing healthy replica is delayed, which is the real issue (the replica already has its own local copy of the data, it just doesn't get promoted fast enough) What I've checked so far: Anti-affinity is correctly set — replicas are on different nodes numberOfInstances: 3 This isn't specific to my local-storage choice — I found a similar report (zalando/postgres-operator#556) with the same symptom on network storage: node killed = no failover for minutes What I'm trying to figure out: Is there a recommended Patroni TTL / retry_timeout / loop_wait config to shrink this detection window, independent of Kubernetes' own node-eviction timers? Is there a standard way to speed up the K8s-side detection ( node-monitor-grace-period , pod-eviction-timeout ) safely in a small on-prem/hybrid cluster without causing false-positive evictions on flaky links? Anyone running Patroni HA on bare local storage (no Ceph/Longhorn) in production who's solved this cleanly — external node-health watchdog + forced node deletion? Or is that considered an anti-pattern and I should bite the bullet on network-replicated storage (Ceph/Longhorn) despite the latency cost, purely to unblock faster rescheduling?
